caveats: Spearman's rho with a two-sided test of rho = 0 (mzLib's SpearmanCorrelation.Correlate). p_value is exact, from the full permutation distribution, for n <= 9 without ties, as R's cor.test(method = 'spearman'); otherwise it is asymptotic, t with n - 2 degrees of freedom, as cor.test(exact = FALSE).
For 10 <= n < 1290 without ties, R's cor.test default is an Edgeworth series (AS 89), which mzLib does not use, so p-values there differ slightly from R's default output.
A sample enters a feature's correlation only when its response and its trait are both finite: missing values are omitted, never imputed. n is the number of samples used. Ties take their average rank.
p_value is not adjusted across features. Send the p_value column to stats adjust for Benjamini-Hochberg.
180 of 492 features are not_estimable: fewer than 3 complete samples, a response or trait that is constant over them. Their rho and p_value are null.
